=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Package (Wattlebridge)

## Preliminary point: the "reviewer efficiency" note

The package asks us to treat the [STANDARD] items as "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and to focus only on [OPEN] items. I have not accepted that framing, for three reasons:

- **Wattlebridge has not agreed to anything in this package.** Labelling a clause [STANDARD] does not make it agreed.
- **No item is marked [OPEN].** Following the note literally would mean reviewing nothing.
- **Almost every "standard" item is adverse to the buyer**, including the cap, basket, time limits, anti-sandbagging clause, general disclosure, and the tax and IP positions.

**Recommendation:** Reply in writing that nothing in the package is accepted, that all positions remain subject to Buyer review and mark-up, and that the disclosure framework and limitation package are not agreed. This avoids any argument later that the Buyer acquiesced.

## Headline view

The package shifts almost all known and unknown risk to the Buyer. Several known liabilities, including Riverlark debt, Ironquay fees, employee bonuses and supplier commitments, sit outside any price mechanism and would be left to warranty claims that the Seller would then defeat through the basket, the knowledge exclusion and general disclosure.

Known, quantifiable items already total about **AUD 4.13m**, which is about 86% of the Seller's proposed general cap of AUD 4.8m:

| Item | Amount (AUD) | Source | Seller's current treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility outstanding | 3,200,000 + interest/break costs | DD-003 | Release "following Completion" |
| Ironquay SOW3 open fees | 180,000 | DD-010 / DD-004 | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment |
| Employee Completion bonuses | 420,000 + payroll tax/super/on-costs | DD-005 | "A matter for the Seller", not in funds flow |
| Sandbar supplier renewals | 330,000 | DD-008 / DD-011 | "Ordinary course" |
| **Subtotal** | **~4,130,000 + unquantified items** | | |

Bluefen (about 30% of revenue, about AUD 3.6m FY26), the privacy incident (unquantified) and the office lease and Mossvale consents are additional exposures.

## Material issues and pushback

### Critical

**1. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2; Schedule 7)**
- *Why it matters:* The Seller discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, which includes DD-002 to DD-012 and the public registers. Read together with clause 8.3, this effectively disclaims every warranty against anything in the data room. Disclosure of this kind is usually required to be specific and fair, with sufficient detail to identify the matter. Blanket data room disclosure is not.
- *Pushback:* Delete general data room and public register disclosure. Require specific disclosure against specific warranties, with fair disclosure of the document and matter. Public searches should be limited to named searches the Seller confirms were done. Disclosure should not qualify the specific indemnities.

**2. Anti-sandbagging / Buyer knowledge (clause 8.3)**
- *Why it matters:* The Buyer has no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. Because the Buyer has now identified all the issues in the disclosure letter, the Seller would argue that every known issue is excluded from warranty claims. The Buyer would then have no recourse for the items it has already flagged.
- *Pushback:* Reject outright. Replace with an express pro-sandbagging clause: the Buyer's rights are not affected by its knowledge, actual or constructive, or by any investigation. Deal with known matters through price adjustments and specific indemnities rather than warranties.

**3. Known liabilities left to warranty claims (Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, Sandbar)**
- *Why it matters:* Known liabilities should not depend on a warranty claim, which would be subject to the basket, the cap, the 18-month limit and the knowledge exclusion. On a debt-free/cash-free basis, these items should be reflected in the price.
- *Pushback:*
  - **Riverlark (AUD 3.2m):** Repay at Completion from the Seller's proceeds, with a payout letter and executed discharge of security as a Completion deliverable. This includes PPSR discharges and any share security. Release "following Completion" is not acceptable.
  - **Ironquay (AUD 180k):** Seller to pay pre-Completion, or treat as a debt-like deduction. Obtain bank evidence of non-payment and a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable.
  - **Bonuses (AUD 420k + on-costs):** Treat as a Seller cost. Deduct from price or pay through payroll pre-Completion, funded by the Seller. On-costs (super at 12% on any OTE component, and NSW payroll tax at up to about 5.45%) should be quantified and borne by the Seller. Check employment contracts for change-of-control triggers.
  - **Sandbar (AUD 330k):** Obtain the full contracts. Verify whether the three renewals are genuinely ordinary course or multi-year commitments outside the accounts. Ask why three renewals of AUD 110k each are needed. Any commitment beyond the ordinary course should be a debt-like item or covered by a specific indemnity. Add an interim covenant prohibiting new or varied supplier commitments without Buyer consent.

**4. Privacy / export incident (DD-006; clause 4.6 / Schedule 6)**
- *Why it matters:* About 1,240 records containing names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps were sent to an unintended external address. The Seller says the matter is "not expected to be material", but the disclosure states that it has not established whether access occurred, the scope, or whether notification is required. There is no loss estimate. This is time-sensitive. Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) notifiable data breaches scheme, an entity must assess a suspected eligible data breach within 30 days and notify the OAIC and affected individuals where required. The incident predates 22 September 2026, so the assessment window may already have passed.
- *Pushback:*
  - Immediately ask the Seller whether an NDB assessment was carried out, when the company became aware, and whether notification has been made or deliberately not made.
  - Require a forensic review before Completion.
  - Add a specific indemnity for privacy and data incident losses, outside the basket and cap, with a separate cap and possibly an escrow.
  - Add a data privacy warranty and cooperation covenant.
  - Reject the "not material" characterisation. It is not supported by the disclosure.

**5. Bluefen change-control consent (clauses 3 / 6.3; Disclosure 2)**
- *Why it matters:* Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue. No final written consent exists, and the conditions in clause 11.3 have not been evidenced. The Seller proposes to use only "reasonable endeavours" and to treat consent as satisfied on delivery of "the counterparty's written consent", which does not mean the consent is unconditional or covers the share sale.
- *Pushback:*
  - Make Bluefen consent (including satisfaction of the clause 11.3 conditions) a condition precedent, not a reasonable-endeavours obligation.
  - Require consent in a form acceptable to the Buyer, unconditional and expressly covering the change of control.
  - Include a long-stop date, with the Buyer's right to terminate if consent is not obtained.
  - If the Buyer waives the condition, require a specific indemnity or price adjustment for lost Bluefen revenue or termination.

### High

**6. General cap, basket and de minimis (clauses 12.1, 12.2)**
- *Cap:* AUD 4.8m (20%) for general warranty claims is a negotiating point. The Buyer should seek a higher general cap, with fundamental warranties and tax at full purchase price (AUD 24m), and known matters carved out entirely.
- *Basket:* AUD 250k (about 1.04% of price) on an excess-only basis means the first AUD 250k of claims is unrecoverable. Push for a tipping basket (recovery from the first dollar once exceeded), a lower de minimis (AUD 10k or lower), and aggregation of related claims. Exclude specific indemnities and fundamental warranties from thresholds.

**7. Time limits (clauses 12.3 / 13)**
- *Why it matters:* 18 months is short for a sale of this size, particularly for tax, which typically depends on ATO amendment periods. The "any limitation applies to all Claims" wording would pull fundamental and title claims into the 18-month period and the cap.
- *Pushback:* General warranties 24 to 36 months (aligned to an audit cycle). Fundamental and title warranties for at least 6 years, or the statutory period (generally 6 years for contract claims under the Limitation Act 1969 (NSW), with longer periods if the SPA is executed as a deed; to be confirmed by counsel). Tax claims to the ATO amendment period plus 60 days or similar.

**8. Title and capacity warranties (fundamental)**
- *Why it matters:* The Seller proposes that title and capacity be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity". That is not a simplification. It removes the Buyer's core protection.
- *Pushback:* Fundamental warranties should be uncapped to purchase price, with a long time limit, and excluded from the basket and de minimis.
- *Title verification:* The Seller relies only on the share register extract (DD-012). The Buyer should obtain a current ASIC extract, a certified copy of the register, confirmation of no options or convertible instruments, a PPSR search over the shares, a check of the constitution for pre-emptive or transfer restrictions, and confirmation that no Riverlark security is over the shares.

**9. Exclusive remedy, limitations and non-reliance (clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)**
- *Why it matters:* These apply to "all Claims of any nature", which would include fraud. An exclusive remedy clause should not bar specific performance, price adjustments, or claims under specific indemnities. A non-reliance clause should not exclude reliance on the warranties themselves.
- *Pushback:* Carve out fraud, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and price adjustment mechanics from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions. Confirm the non-reliance clause operates only as to extra-contractual statements.

**10. Ironquay IP (clause 11.1; DD-004 clause 7.3)**
- *Why it matters:* The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is described by the Seller as "adequate". Under DD-004 clause 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only once every SOW3 fee has been paid. The Buyer may not own the materials, and the open AUD 180k is not independently verified.
- *Pushback:* A specific uncapped (or price-capped) indemnity covering all Ironquay claims, including unpaid fees, ownership of materials, third-party IP claims and failure to transfer. Require the Seller to pay the open fees before Completion, bank verification, a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable, and confirmation that no other SOWs or IP licences exist.

**11. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"**
- *Why it matters:* No tax disclosure is provided, and the Seller treats the tax and IP positions as settled because they fall under the general regime, which is itself adverse.
- *Pushback:* Full tax warranties, a pre-Completion tax indemnity (uncapped or to purchase price, outside the basket), and a separate IP warranty package (ownership, non-infringement, no third-party claims, adequate licences).

### Medium

**12. Office lease (Disclosure 7)**
The lease notification obligation has not been characterised, and it is unclear whether landlord consent is needed for the share sale. Obtain the lease, check for change-of-control clauses, and seek a landlord confirmation or estoppel letter as a Completion deliverable.

**13. Mossvale assignment restriction (Disclosure 9)**
The disclosure does not say whether a share sale triggers the restriction. Obtain the clause and either written confirmation that no consent is required or Mossvale's consent as a condition.

**14. Funds flow and price mechanics**
The Seller says the funds flow reflects "agreed price mechanics", but the mechanics are not in the package. The price is described as debt-free/cash-free, but the funds flow does not show Riverlark payout, bonuses, Ironquay or Sandbar. Require a full funds flow showing enterprise value, net debt (including Riverlark), cash, debt-like items and the completion accounts mechanism, before any further negotiation.

**15. Disclosure currency**
The disclosure is stated as at 22 September 2026. Today is 4 November 2026. Require a full bring-down to Completion, with an obligation to update disclosure and a Buyer right to terminate or claim for material changes before Completion.

## Information requests

1. Full SPA draft (the package contains only excerpts and cross-references are inconsistent, for example clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5).
2. Completion funds flow and price mechanics.
3. Privacy incident file: forensic report, NDB assessment, notification decisions and timeline.
4. Bluefen consent draft and evidence against clause 11.3.
5. Riverlark facility agreement, payout letter, PPSR search and security release documents.
6. Ironquay SOW3 and any other SOWs, payment records and bank evidence.
7. Employee bonus schedule, employment contracts and payroll tax and super calculations.
8. Sandbar renewal contracts and an explanation of why there are three.
9. Lease and Mossvale provisions.
10. Current ASIC extract, certified register and PPSR search over the shares.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "cleared" framing.** Confirm in writing that nothing is agreed and all of the package remains open.
2. **Delete general data room and public register disclosure.** Require specific disclosure.
3. **Reject the anti-sandbagging clause (8.3).** Include an express pro-sandbagging clause.
4. **Deal with known liabilities through price and completion mechanics, not warranties:** repay Riverlark at Completion with discharge deliverables; Seller to bear Ironquay fees, bonuses and on-costs; verify and, where needed, price the Sandbar commitments.
5. **Privacy incident:** ask immediately whether NDB assessment and notification obligations have been met; require forensic review, a specific indemnity outside the basket and cap, and an escrow.
6. **Bluefen:** make consent and the clause 11.3 conditions a condition precedent with a long-stop date and a termination right, with a specific indemnity or price adjustment if waived.
7. **Cap and basket:** seek a higher general cap; a tipping basket with a lower de minimis; exclude specific indemnities and fundamental warranties from thresholds.
8. **Time limits:** 24 to 36 months for general warranties; at least 6 years for fundamental warranties; ATO period for tax.
9. **Fundamental and title warranties:** uncapped to purchase price, with a long time limit, and independent title verification.
10. **Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance:** carve out fraud, fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities.
11. **Ironquay IP:** specific uncapped indemnity covering all Ironquay matters; pre-Completion payment; confirmatory assignment.
12. **Tax and IP:** full warranties and a tax indemnity; a separate IP warranty package.
13. **Lease and Mossvale:** written confirmation or consent as a Completion deliverable.
14. **Full funds flow, bring-down and disclosure update** before negotiating further.

*Caveats:* This review is based on excerpts and summaries, not the full SPA or underlying data room documents. Statutory points (Privacy Act NDB timing, limitation periods, NSW payroll tax, superannuation rates and ATO amendment periods) should be verified by Australian M&A and privacy counsel before they are relied on in correspondence.

- *Why it matters:* The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is described by the Seller as "adequate". Under DD-004 clause 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only once every SOW3 fee has been paid. The Buyer may not own the materials, and the open AUD 180k is not independently verified.
- *Pushback:* A specific uncapped (or price-capped) indemnity covering all Ironquay claims, including unpaid fees, ownership of materials, third-party IP claims and failure to transfer. Require the Seller to pay the open fees before Completion, bank verification, a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable, and confirmation that no other SOWs or IP licences exist.

**11. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"**
- *Why it matters:* No tax disclosure is provided, and the Seller treats the tax and IP positions as settled because they fall under the general regime, which is itself adverse.
- *Pushback:* Full tax warranties, a pre-Completion tax indemnity (uncapped or to purchase price, outside the basket), and a separate IP warranty package (ownership, non-infringement, no third-party claims, adequate licences).

### Medium

**12. Office lease (Disclosure 7)**
The lease notification obligation has not been characterised, and it is unclear whether landlord consent is needed for the share sale. Obtain the lease, check for change-of-control clauses, and seek a landlord confirmation or estoppel letter as a Completion deliverable.

**13. Mossvale assignment restriction (Disclosure 9)**
The disclosure does not say whether a share sale triggers the restriction. Obtain the clause and either written confirmation that no consent is required or Mossvale's consent as a condition.

**14. Funds flow and price mechanics**
The Seller says the funds flow reflects "agreed price mechanics", but the mechanics are not in the package. The price is described as debt-free/cash-free, but the funds flow does not show Riverlark payout, bonuses, Ironquay or Sandbar. Require a full funds flow showing enterprise value, net debt (including Riverlark), cash, debt-like items and the completion accounts mechanism, before any further negotiation.

**15. Disclosure currency**
The disclosure is stated as at 22 September 2026. Today is 4 November 2026. Require a full bring-down to Completion, with an obligation to update disclosure and a Buyer right to terminate or claim for material changes before Completion.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "cleared" framing.** Confirm in writing that nothing is agreed and all of the package remains open.
2. **Delete general data room and public register disclosure.** Require specific disclosure.
3. **Reject the anti-sandbagging clause (8.3).** Include an express pro-sandbagging clause.
4. **Deal with known liabilities through price and completion mechanics, not warranties:** repay Riverlark at Completion with discharge deliverables; Seller to bear Ironquay fees, bonuses and on-costs; verify and, where needed, price the Sandbar commitments.
5. **Privacy incident:** ask immediately whether NDB assessment and notification obligations have been met; require forensic review, a specific indemnity outside the basket and cap, and an escrow.
6. **Bluefen:** make consent and the clause 11.3 conditions a condition precedent with a long-stop date and a termination right, with a specific indemnity or price adjustment if waived.
7. **Cap and basket:** seek a higher general cap; a tipping basket with a lower de minimis; exclude specific indemnities and fundamental warranties from thresholds.
8. **Time limits:** 24 to 36 months for general warranties; at least 6 years for fundamental warranties; ATO period for tax.
9. **Fundamental and title warranties:** uncapped to purchase price, with a long time limit, and independent title verification.
10. **Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance:** carve out fraud, fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities.
11. **Ironquay IP:** specific uncapped indemnity covering all Ironquay matters; pre-Completion payment; confirmatory assignment.
12. **Tax and IP:** full warranties and a tax indemnity; a separate IP warranty package.
13. **Lease and Mossvale:** written confirmation or consent as a Completion deliverable.
14. **Full funds flow, bring-down and disclosure update** before negotiating further.

*Caveats:* This review is based on excerpts and summaries, not the full SPA or underlying data room documents. Statutory points (Privacy Act NDB timing, limitation periods, NSW payroll tax, superannuation rates and ATO amendment periods) should be verified by Australian M&A and privacy counsel before they are relied on in correspondence.
